Definition: properly, a cliff (or sharp rock, as compressed); generally, a rock or boulder; figuratively, a refuge; also an edge (as precipitous)
BiblicalUsage: Scripture uses tsûwr where it means a rock. In Exodus 17:6, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb. That is the sense it carries through all 74 of its occurrences.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that the Rock is not a picture I chose for God; it is the name He gives Himself, and no other ground holds. That is why I read the passages around tsûwr slowly, instead of hurrying past.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
